title: Weyba Bridge

bikeon.heading: Weyba Bridge
paras: Weyba Creek winds from Lake Weyba, the southern gateway to the Noosa Everglades system, to meet the lower Noosa River. Bridging it has always been a saga. The first, the 61 m Alexandra Bridge, opened in 1886 and was soon ruined by shipworm. A timber pile bridge opened on 19 October 1929, the same day as the Doonella bridge, finally linking Tewantin, Noosaville and Noosa Heads by road. When a concrete bridge replaced it from 1969, locals kept the old one for walkers. It partly collapsed in 1991, and the Friends of the Old Weyba Bridge raised money for the replica you ride today, built in 1995. The creek is part of the Noosa River Fish Habitat Area, its mangroves a nursery for fish, crabs and prawns. Weyba is understood to mean place of stingrays in the Kabi Kabi language.

story: Weyba Creek winds from Lake Weyba, the southern gateway to the Noosa Everglades system, down to the Noosa River. Bridging it has always been a saga.

The first bridge opened in 1886 and was soon ruined by shipworm. A timber bridge opened in October 1929, the same day as the Doonella bridge, and at last Tewantin, Noosaville and Noosa Heads were joined by road.
When a concrete bridge took over from 1969, locals kept the old one for walkers. It partly collapsed in 1991, and a community group raised the money for the replica you are riding on, built in 1995.
The mangroves here are a nursery for fish, crabs and prawns. Weyba is understood to mean place of stingrays in the Kabi Kabi language.
